fullPassage: Researchers predicted that a plant may react to diminished resource availability caused by a nearby plant by putting more energy into growing its roots directly below its stem. The potential for this strategy to increase root volume would maximize its fitness, they theorized, but could result in a “tragedy of the commons” situation in which intense competition leads to the eventual depletion of moisture and nutrients in the soil, ultimately compromising the plant’s survival. An experiment conducted to test the theory found that when pepper plants were grown close to each other, they did adjust by growing their roots directly beneath themselves, investing heavily in their root systems to compete for underground resources. This was more likely to occur the closer the plants were to one another. Though this strategy optimized the ability of plants to obtain resources, as predicted, the “tragedy of the commons” scenario did not arise.
